answers.stem_only: Workforce access to many accounts in an organization with single sign-on and short-term CLI credentials: enable IAM Identity Center, connect the existing SAML 2.0 IdP as an external identity source, and assign permission sets to the accounts; engineers use aws sso login for the CLI. The customer mobile app is irrelevant to this requirement.

Add a Cognito identity pool that trusts the existing user pool as its provider; the identity pool exchanges the user pool token for temporary credentials of the authenticated IAM role, and that role's policy limits s3:PutObject to the prefix built from the policy variable ${cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:sub} so each customer can write only to their own prefix.

AD Connector in the VPC: a proxy that forwards authentication to the reachable on-premises domain controllers, stores no users in AWS, and is supported by Amazon WorkSpaces. Register it with WorkSpaces.

IAM Identity Center has one identity source at a time, so change the identity source from AD Connector to an external identity provider and set up SAML 2.0 between Okta and Identity Center; then enable automatic provisioning (SCIM) in Identity Center and configure Okta with the SCIM endpoint and access token so new hires are created automatically.

Customer identity, not workforce: an Amazon Cognito user pool with Google as a social identity provider for sign-in, plus a Cognito identity pool that exchanges the user pool token for temporary AWS credentials of an IAM role allowed to upload to S3. The employee SAML IdP and the 12 accounts are context only.

Use the AWS Directory Service feature for AWS Management Console access: create an access URL (alias) for the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory, enable console access, and assign an IAM role to the administrators' directory group; they sign in at the access URL with directory credentials. An account instance of IAM Identity Center cannot grant AWS account access with permission sets, and creating an organization is more overhead.

RDS for SQL Server Windows Authentication works with AWS Managed Microsoft AD (AD Connector and Simple AD are not supported). Create AWS Managed Microsoft AD in the VPC, join the DB instance to it, and create a forest trust with the on-premises domain so existing on-premises AD accounts can authenticate. (RDS also supports joining a self-managed AD directly, but that is not about running extra domain controllers on EC2.)

IAM Identity Center accepts only one identity source and AD Connector serves one domain. Create AWS Managed Microsoft AD in the management account, create a two-way forest trust to each on-premises forest (Identity Center needs two-way trusts to reach users in trusted domains), and set the managed directory as the single identity source.

Use the ALB built-in authentication: create a Cognito user pool, add each customer's SAML 2.0 IdP to it, and add an authenticate-cognito action before the forward action in the rules of the existing HTTPS listener (authenticate actions work only on HTTPS listeners). No application code changes.

IAM Identity Center provisions the permission set into the member account as an IAM role named AWSReservedSSO_<permission set name>_<suffix>, trusted by the account's SAML provider for Identity Center, with the AWS managed read-only policy attached. No IAM users or groups are created.

A Cognito identity pool with unauthenticated (guest) access enabled; it issues temporary credentials for the unauthenticated IAM role, whose policy allows the DynamoDB writes. Later the same identity pool can add authenticated identities.

Create an API Gateway authorizer of type COGNITO_USER_POOLS that points to the user pool, enable it on the API methods, and have the client send the user pool ID or access token in the Authorization header. API Gateway validates the token with no custom code.
